userStories.title: Broken object-level authorization — ask_orchestrator trusts client _run_id/_task_id and loads/mutates tasks with no workspace/run scoping
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (HIGH, verified end-to-end). The handler docstring and the executor comment both claim the caller subject is 'server-injected, never a tool parameter; a client-supplied run_id/task_id is ignored'. That is only true in the real mission lane, where coordinator_service.py:2296-2308 now always threads field_context={run_id,task_id,agent_id}. It is NOT true in five OTHER execute_with_prompt lanes that pass no context_mode: agent_factory.py:1004 defaults the mode to TASK_EXECUTION, so ask_orchestrator is EXPOSED in api/board_tasks.py:1168, api/composio.py:839, api/webhooks.py:992, services/scheduled_task_service.py:426, and channels/base.py:170 (the last feeds EXTERNAL attacker-controlled content, envelope.content). Those lanes pass a context with no run_id/field_id, so agent_factory.py:1192-1197 builds field_context=None, and the executor's ask_orchestrator binding block (platform_executor.py:1099-1104) only CONDITIONALLY injects (if fctx value is not None) and — unlike exec_platform's _agent_id handling (exec_platform.py:66-69, which strips-then-injects) — never STRIPS a client-supplied value first. The LLM params reach the handler unfiltered: via platform_execute, unified_executor.py:708-741 validates only that 'question' is present (no additionalProperties:false, no key filtering) and forwards the raw params object. Then handlers_clarify.py:112-125 (_load_task) and orchestrator_answers.py:204-249 (_upstream_blocks) query OrchestrationTask by id with NO workspace/run filter (OrchestrationTask has no workspace_id column). Failure scenario: an agent in a channel/webhook/board/scheduled lane is prompt-injected to call platform_execute with params={question:..., _run_id:<x>, _task_id:<uuid of a task in workspace B>}; _upstream_blocks returns that task's dependency outputs as a 'grounded, cited' answer (cross-tenant read) and _park_task_with_draft writes DRAFT_KEY/PENDING_KEY onto that task's JSONB (cross-tenant write). Gated behind knowing a victim task UUID, hence HIGH not CRITICAL — but the authorization check is genuinely missing and reachable. FIX: mirror the established _agent_id pattern — strip client _run_id/_task_id/_field_id at the executor chokepoint before injecting from field_context, AND scope the task read to the server subject.

userStories.title: NO_ANSWER sentinel matched by exact-string equality — a non-conforming declination leaks as a grounded, cited answer
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified; fabrication-adjacent — this platform's known failure family, PRD-223). orchestrator_answers.py:131 guards the composition reply with `if not answer or answer.strip() == _NO_ANSWER:`. The system prompt (:377-383) tells the LLM to reply 'exactly NO_ANSWER and nothing else', but nothing enforces the format. If the model appends punctuation or a caveat or markdown ('NO_ANSWER — the context does not cover this', '**NO_ANSWER**'), the exact-equality check fails, the guard falls through, and the declination text itself becomes result['answer'] WITH sources attached (:135-137) — a cited, confident-looking answer that is really a refusal, which also defeats the cannot_answer -> escalation path. Only the verbatim string is exercised by the suite (test_no_answer_sentinel_is_cannot_answer). FIX: robust sentinel detection (e.g. treat a reply whose normalized/upper form starts with or contains NO_ANSWER as cannot_answer).
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — answer_clarification now guards with _is_no_answer(answer) instead of `answer.strip() == _NO_ANSWER`. _is_no_answer uppercases + lstrips surrounding markup (_SENTINEL_LEADING = markdown emphasis/blockquote/list/quote/space) then tests startswith(NO_ANSWER), so any reply LEADING with the sentinel in a non-bare form declines; a mid-sentence mention in a genuine answer does not.

DONE — test_no_answer_near_miss_is_cannot_answer parametrized over ['NO_ANSWER','NO_ANSWER.','**NO_ANSWER**','NO_ANSWER - not in context','NO_ANSWER — the context does not cover this','> NO_ANSWER','no_answer'] → all {cannot_answer, unretrievable} with stub.calls==1 (no leaked sources); test_genuine_answer_mentioning_sentinel_is_returned proves a real answer that mentions NO_ANSWER mid-sentence still returns with sources + CLARIFICATION_ANSWERED; test_is_no_answer_unit covers the matcher directly.

DONE — cd orchestrator && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_prd229_orchestrator_answers.py → 28 passed (was 19; +9 RVW-3). Genuine regression guard: the old exact-equality check returned 'NO_ANSWER.' etc. as a cited answer — these tests fail without the fix.

userStories.title: CLARIFICATION_BUDGET check is a non-atomic read-then-write — concurrent asks in one run can exceed the budget
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified; low blast radius). orchestrator_answers.py:116-118 checks _answers_used() (a COUNT of CLARIFICATION_ANSWERED events, :170-186) and only later _record()s the answer via emit_event INSERT (:430-459) — two unlocked operations. Tasks in one run execute concurrently (coordinator_service._run_agent_io via asyncio.gather; dispatcher dispatches up to max_concurrent). Two tasks calling ask_orchestrator at once can both read the same pre-increment count, both pass the >= budget check, and both answer — the run's answered count can exceed Config.CLARIFICATION_BUDGET by the degree of concurrency. Impact is cost-control softness (default budget 3), not correctness or security, so this is a low-priority hardening. FIX: make the budget spend atomic (e.g. count+record under a per-run guard, or a conditional insert), or explicitly accept the soft cap with a comment noting the race is bounded by max_concurrent.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE (soft-cap branch, per AC's OR) — the check site now carries a mechanism-grounded SOFT-CAP note with the max_concurrent bound. The atomic branch is architecturally UNSAFE here: concurrent asks run agent I/O on SEPARATE DB sessions (coordinator_service Phase 2 asyncio.gather), emit_event FLUSHES without COMMIT, and READ COMMITTED sees only committed rows — so no app/advisory lock closes the window without committing a borrowed agent-runtime session mid-tool-execution (durably persisting its unrelated pending work — a worse bug); a schema-encoded slot/separate counter is barred by PRD-229's zero-migration + 'count off the event trail' design. Overspend is bounded by max_concurrent (default 3), pure cost-control softness — escalations are never budget-limited.

DONE (N/A — atomic branch not taken) — AC1's OR (documented soft cap) was chosen with the architectural justification above, so the atomic-only 'one answers, other escalates' test does not apply. Instead test_budget_soft_cap_is_bounded_by_committed_trail PINS the accepted contract: two asks on the same committed baseline (budget-1) both answer (bounded overspend), and once the trail COMMITS to budget the next declines WITHOUT composing (stub.calls unchanged) — so a future atomic change must consciously flip this test + the doc.
DONE — cd orchestrator && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_prd229_orchestrator_answers.py → 29 passed (+1 RVW-4).

userStories.title: HIGH — escalation park+draft is neither committed nor exception-safe: a sibling task's rollback silently destroys the draft and orphans the human ask
userStories.description: SUPERVISOR-FILED from a targeted security review (the automated reviewer crashed 3x and never reached this). VERIFIED SHARED SESSION: coordinator_service.py:2242 builds AgentFactory(db_session=db) per task inside _prepare_task, all from ONE SessionLocal() opened at :1521, and Phase 2 runs them CONCURRENTLY via asyncio.gather (:1740-1750) — so orchestrator_answers.py:128-134's comment claiming 'concurrent tasks run on SEPARATE DB sessions' is factually wrong and must be corrected. DEFECT: clarification_ladder.py escalate_clarification (:35-76) calls ask_human (:60) which durably COMMITS the grant (human sees the ask / gets the Telegram ping), then _park_task_with_draft (:64, mutating output_metadata[DRAFT_KEY] + input_context[PENDING_KEY] at :96-103) and _record_escalation (:67) only flush — never commit. FAILURE: sibling task B's unrelated tool error fires platform_executor.py:1244-1247 db.rollback() on the SHARED session, wiping task A's uncommitted draft + PENDING_KEY while the human-visible ask survives → an orphaned ask no answer can ever bridge back, and Gerard's baked 'draft on park' decision silently lost with nothing logged. SECOND DEFECT: handlers_clarify.py:93-109 does not wrap escalate_clarification, so a throw AFTER ask_human committed returns a bare {'success': False} to the agent even though a human WAS asked — a naive retry files a duplicate ask. FIX: (a) commit immediately after _park_task_with_draft, mirroring ask_human's own durably-park-first pattern; (b) wrap the escalation call in handlers_clarify so a post-ask_human failure reports the ask as PLACED rather than as a failure; (c) correct the incorrect session comment in orchestrator_answers.py:128-134.

userStories.title: HIGH — a parked task is not held: record_task_completion clobbers the draft and completes it, and apply_answered_clarification has zero production callers so the human answer can never resume
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (HIGH, verified end-to-end; DISTINCT from P229-RVW-5's uncommitted-draft/rollback angle — this occurs even after RVW-5 commits the draft). escalate_clarification writes a draft + PENDING_KEY and returns {parked} so the agent stops (clarification_ladder.py:64,79-103), but NOTHING in the coordinator holds the task. After the agent tool loop returns, coordinator_service.py:1764 UNCONDITIONALLY calls _record_task_result -> dispatcher.record_task_completion (coordinator_service.py:2381) with NO pending_ask_id() check. On success that path FULL-REPLACES output_metadata (dispatcher.py:759 — a brand-new dict, wiping the clarification_draft key) and transitions the task to COMPLETED (dispatcher.py:771). apply_answered_clarification/pending_ask_id have ZERO production callers (grep: only tests; render_resume_block at dispatcher.py:939 reads RESUME_KEY, which ONLY apply_answered_clarification sets, so the resume block is dead code in the live flow). NET, reachable now (the tool is live in TASK_EXECUTION — modes.py:34,38): a mission agent that calls platform_ask_orchestrator and escalates gets a real, human-notifying ask_human grant, then the task COMPLETES with the agent's post-park text as PERMANENT output (consumed by downstream dependent tasks) and the draft is wiped — the human's answer can never resume the work. This is the auto-hold/rerun gap surfaced in US-003 AC5, but the surfacing understated it: the tool is live-exposed while escalation actively ORPHANS human asks and DEGRADES task output, not merely 'not yet wired'. FIX closes the REACHABLE HARM only — the full auto-hold/rerun dispatch surgery stays Gerard's call (US-003 AC5 flags stall-detection/infinite-loop interactions needing the real loop + integration tests; do NOT wire it blind).

userStories.title: MEDIUM — governance keyword backstop misses common phrasings, so spend/destructive/scope questions can be auto-answered instead of escalated
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified). Governance detection = caller-declared category (optional, LLM-self-declared, advisory — actions_clarify.py:52-60) OR a conservative substring scan (_GOVERNANCE_KEYWORDS orchestrator_answers.py:54-67; _governance_category :168-180). The substring list has real gaps for natural phrasing: spend lacks cost/expense/fee/billing and matches 'budget increase' only in that word order (so 'increase the budget' misses); destructive lacks overwrite/revoke/deactivate/reformat/uninstall; scope needs verbatim 'scope change'/'out of scope' (so 'should I also fix X while I am here?' misses). FAILURE: platform_ask_orchestrator(question='Should I increase the compute budget for this task?', category=None) -> _governance_category returns None -> ordinary clarification -> Auto composes a grounded, cited answer on a SPEND decision with no human in the loop. The answer is grounded (not a fabrication) and downstream approval gates still apply (PRD-229 §4), so this is a hardening of the escalate-governance guarantee (G3), not a fabrication. Existing governance tests exercise only verbatim keywords (delete/purchase/scope change). FIX: broaden keyword coverage and add a natural-phrasing fixture that must escalate.

userStories.title: MEDIUM — no per-task cap on platform_ask_orchestrator rounds: N slow answer rounds can consume most of the task envelope (the 30s box bounds ONE call only)
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified). CLARIFICATION_ANSWER_TIMEOUT (config.py, 30s) bounds a SINGLE answer round (handlers_clarify.py:74-78 asyncio.wait_for). CLARIFICATION_BUDGET (3) caps ANSWERED rounds per RUN (not per task), and cannot_answer/escalate rounds are unlimited by design. So one light-mode task (max_tool_iterations=5, timeout_seconds=120 — coordinator_service.py:92) can spend up to 3 near-30s answered rounds = ~90s of its 120s asyncio.wait_for envelope on clarifications alone, before its own LLM turns; the outer envelope then hard-cancels the ENTIRE task (lost work + retry) instead of gracefully declining a round. The config comment ('30s sits well inside the smallest envelope … can never blow the task timeout') and the only test (test_prd229_ask_orchestrator.py — asserts 0 < timeout < 120) reason about a SINGLE call, not the N the tool permits per task. Low-probability (needs near-max timings) but real. FIX: bound the CUMULATIVE clarification time or count per task (a per-task call cap, or subtract elapsed clarification time from the remaining envelope) so N rounds cannot approach the envelope; update the config comment to state the per-task bound.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — CLARIFICATION_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_TASK (config.py:963, default 2, via config.py's own os.getenv — canonical config only) bounds the answer rounds a SINGLE task may ENTER. userStories.title: MEDIUM — every retrieved block is reported as a source, not the subset the model cited — weakens the grounded/cited guarantee
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified). answer_clarification returns sources = [b['source'] for b in blocks] (orchestrator_answers.py:159) — EVERY retrieved block (up to _MAX_BLOCKS=12, spanning upstream/field/memory/corpus/fleet), regardless of whether the composition used it. The system prompt asks the model to 'Cite the [n] blocks you used' (:409-415) but nothing parses the [n] markers back against sources, and _upstream_blocks includes every upstream dependency output with no relevance filter (:228-281). Every source IS a real retrieved ref (not a fabrication), but an answer composed from 1 of 12 blocks still reports all 12 as its grounding — over-claiming the 'every answer carries the source refs it was grounded on' guarantee the module docstring makes, and misleading any downstream audit/UI that treats sources as 'what was actually used'. Tests cover only the single-block happy path. FIX: parse the model's [n] citations and return only the cited blocks' sources (fall back to all only when the model cited none), OR rename/document the field as the retrieved-context set rather than the cited subset.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — chose the PARSE contract: _cited_sources (orchestrator_answers.py:499) parses the answer's [n] markers (1-based, as _build_messages numbers the blocks) back to blocks in first-cited order, de-duped by index, ignoring out-of-range markers (never invents a source). sources = _cited_sources(answer, blocks) at :179 (was `[b['source'] for b in blocks]`). Falls back to ALL retrieved sources ONLY when the answer cited no valid index — so 'sources' now means 'what the answer was grounded on', matching the module docstring's guarantee; it only ever NARROWS, never invents.

userStories.title: LOW/MEDIUM — the workspace-ownership check in _load_task does not gate the upstream-outputs READ it is documented to protect (defence-in-depth gap; not exploitable today)
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (LOW/MEDIUM, verified; NOT independently exploitable). _load_task (handlers_clarify.py:112-148) withholds the task ORM object when the run does not belong to workspace_id, and the comment at orchestrator_answers.py:255-259 claims cross-tenant protection is 'defence in depth behind the executor strip + _load_task scope'. But _upstream_blocks reads subject.task_id/subject.run_id directly (orchestrator_answers.py:234), never subject.task, so _load_task's workspace result only decides whether _park_task_with_draft gets a task to write — it never gates the upstream READ. That read is protected solely by its own OrchestrationTask.run_id==subject.run_id filter (:260) plus the executor strip (_bind_ask_orchestrator_context) that makes run_id/task_id self-consistent from server field_context — hence no live exploit. But the documented defence-in-depth is not actually wired: if workspace_id and the field_context run_id ever diverged (e.g. the known cached-agent-runtime workspace-staleness pattern), _upstream_blocks would read that run's outputs with no workspace check while _external_blocks used the different subject.workspace_id — a split-provenance answer. FIX: scope the _upstream_blocks read through the run->workspace join (make the defence-in-depth real), or correct the comment to claim only the run_id + executor-strip protection it actually has.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — chose the STRONGER option (made the defence real): _upstream_blocks confirms the run belongs to subject.workspace_id BEFORE returning dep outputs (orchestrator_answers.py:291-308). Run loadable + owned by a DIFFERENT workspace → return [] (fail-open ONLY when the run is unloadable — a bogus run_id has no dep outputs to leak, and the run_id fence still applies). The inline run_id-fence comment (:326-333) is corrected to attribute the tenant boundary to THIS run→workspace check + the executor strip, NOT _load_task (grep: 'NOT _load_task' at :333). test_upstream_blocks_refuses_run_owned_by_other_workspace (run in ws-B, subject ws-A → [] — genuine guard: without the check the run_id fence passes and it leaks) + positive twin test_upstream_blocks_allows_run_in_subject_workspace + test_upstream_blocks_fails_open_when_run_unloadable (no run row → run_id fence; the RVW-2 fence tests are unaffected).

userStories.title: Wire the resume loop end-to-end: park → human answers → task resumes
userStories.description: GERARD AUTHORIZED 2026-08-28 (§12 boundary surfaced by the US-003 builder and confirmed by the targeted security review: `apply_answered_clarification` in services/clarification_ladder.py:147-173 has ZERO production callers, so `render_resume_block` at modules/coordination/dispatcher.py:936-943 is a permanent no-op — an agent can ask, a human can answer, and the work NEVER resumes. PRD-229 §6 Wave 1's own acceptance criterion is unmet without this). His words: 'we need to wire it or it's pointless — pause the work, question gets answered, resume'. THREE PARTS. (1) HOLD: the dispatch loop must not re-dispatch a task carrying PENDING_KEY in input_context — it is parked awaiting a human, not ready work. Add the guard where ready tasks are selected (dispatcher.py dispatch_ready path) so a parked task is skipped without being failed or counted as stalled, and its run stays alive rather than completing/failing around it. (2) BRIDGE: when a question-kind ask is ANSWERED (PRD-225's answer path in api/approval_grants.py, which already calls _requeue_subject/_resume_tool_call), detect that the subject is an orchestration task carrying PENDING_KEY and call apply_answered_clarification so RESUME_KEY is set with the Q&A — this is the missing production caller. Reuse 225's existing resume machinery; do NOT build a parallel path. (3) RESUME: the held task becomes dispatchable again once RESUME_KEY is set, and its next run's prompt carries render_resume_block's Q&A block plus the preserved draft (Gerard's baked draft-on-park decision). Interacts with P229-RVW-5: the park write MUST be committed for the hold to survive, so build RVW-5 first or in the same story. Keep the ladder VERTICAL — no lateral agent messaging. ZERO new alembic revisions, no new tables, no new routes (state rides the existing task JSONB, rebuild-don't-mutate).
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — HOLD: dispatch_ready skips PENDING_KEY candidates (dispatcher.py:637-645, P229-RVW-6). A QUEUED-held task is never stall-detected (reconciler stalls only ASSIGNED>60s/RUNNING>300s — the QUEUED-held choice is why, a RUNNING-held task would die at 300s) and a not-all-terminal run with no failed tasks stays RUNNING (reconciler.py:252), so the 5s DB-authoritative tick re-picks it once the marker clears. Tests: test_run_keeps_progress_parked_plus_runnable_sibling + test_dispatch_ready_all_parked_is_no_ready_not_stall (RVW-6) — parked held, not failed, not stalled.

DONE — BRIDGE: api/approval_grants._requeue_subject calls _resume_clarification_if_parked BEFORE _resume_tool_call for tool_call grants (approval_grants.py:367); it discriminates a clarification park precisely (pending_ask_id(task)==grant.id) and bridges via apply_answered_clarification (approval_grants.py:436) — the ONLY production caller (grep: apply_answered_clarification now referenced in api/approval_grants.py, previously tests-only). test_bridge_resumes_clarification_park + test_bridge_declines_non_clarification_tool_call + test_requeue_falls_through_to_resume_tool_call_for_stored_call (PRD-193 not hijacked; 19 existing grant-resume tests green: p2w2_grant_resume + prd225_answer_resume + grant_approve_commit_ordering).

Genuine guard: without the bridge, _resume_tool_call finds no stored action, RESUME_KEY never set, render_resume_block None → asserts fail.
